To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the secondary pre-service teachers in our study perceived that: 1. environmental education was not taught as a separate subject; 2. environmental education was taught as part of other KLAs; 3. environmental education was only taught as a separate topic in the science and geography KLAs; 4. environmental education should be taught in all KLAs; 5. environmental education was more than the teaching of environmental science; 6. environmental education was about the teaching and learning of the environment;
pre-service teachers have a limited understanding of the nature and scope and constraints to the implementation and practice of environmental education.

pre-service teachers in the KLAs of mathematics, science and technology have a narrow view of what constitutes environmental education and have limited awareness of the constraints to the implementation environmental education in schools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how pre-service teachers understand and interpret the role of environmental education in their future classrooms and how this may influence their practice as environmental educators.
the views of pre-service secondary teachers about the nature of environmental education and their views about constraints to the effective implementation of environmental education into practice.
the perceptions held by pre-service teachers about environmental education and the implications for their practice as potential teachers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
environmental education is a complex issue and requires a holistic approach to its implementation in schools.
pre-service teacher education programs should be more explicit about the nature and purpose of environmental education and its place in the curriculum.
pre-service teachers are not being prepared for the reality of environmental education practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the findings of our study have highlighted the need to develop the capacity of pre-service teachers to engage with and understand environmental issues, and to be able to implement the environmental education policy in their future classrooms.
the findings from this study suggest that the perceptions of pre-service teachers are important in understanding the implementation of environmental policy into practice.
pre-service teachers need to be better prepared in their understanding and practice of environmental education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pre-service teachers need opportunities to explore the nature and scope, and the constraints to the implementation, of environmental education policy.

we should be listening to the perceptions of pre-service teachers, as they may be a key to understanding the barriers to the implementation of policy and to the development of environmental educators.
we should not underestimate the importance of listening to pre-service teachers.
